transcript:
Header: 2026-03-18 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sofia (CSM), Jordan (Lunaris), Priya (Lunaris), Carlos (Lunaris)

Summary: quick cost focused review, some noisy audio early. we ran short perf tests last week, today we reviewed numbers and agreed extended run.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, let me do a quick roll call, Ethan and Sofia from Redwood on my side. Jordan?
00:06 Jordan: yep Jordan here, priya and carlos are on as well. sorry audio is a bit echo-y.
00:12 Maya: no worries. so agenda, cost econ review -> tokens per second per dollar, caching results, batching tradeoffs, next actions. Ethan gonna walk through the numbers?
00:22 Ethan: yeah I'll share screen in a sec. quick context: last week we ran 2 short runs with our 8B quantized variant on the dedicated pool and on hosted to compare.
00:32 Jordan: mm-hmm the short runs looked promising, curious about long tail of prompts though.
00:36 Ethan: right, so raw numbers — apologies if the transcription messes up names — baseline hosted (soft quota) run: avg throughput ~ 140 tokens/sec for a single stream on the 8B quantized, that's per connection. Cost measured as $0.28 per 1M tokens in that config. If you normalize, tokens/sec per dollar (rough simple metric) came out to ~500 tokens/sec per $1 for single-stream baseline.
01:02 Priya: can you unpack that metric again, tokens/sec per dollar? our finance asks for cost-per-1k tokens but this helps for throughput planning.
01:10 Ethan: sure, it's a quick way to reason about how many tokens of throughput you get for a unit of spend over the runtime. it's rough since billing is per million tokens but we used it to compare configs.
01:22 Carlos: and what about batching? we saw better throughput with batching in your doc but latency spiked.
01:28 Ethan: yep exactly, we tested batching sizes 4, 8, 16. With batch 8, throughput jumped to ~780 tokens/sec aggregate for the worker (so tokens/sec per $1 goes up to ~2.8k) but p95 latency moved from ~120ms to ~450-700ms depending on route. that's the tradeoff.
01:46 Jordan: so if our product needs sub-200ms for chat UX, big batching may be problematic for interactive flows.
01:52 Maya: correct, that's why we usually recommend hybrid: small batches for interactive routes, big batches for async background jobs.
01:58 Ethan: also caching: with prefix/KV caching turned on (we tested 8MB prefix cache), hit rate on Lunaris sample traffic was ~22% in the short run, which reduced token generation by about 18% and improved effective tokens/sec/$ by roughly the same percent. with a 32MB prefix it jumped to 36% hit rate in the synthetic sample which gave ~31% reduction in token usage.
02:24 Priya: our traffic has a lot of repetitive prompts for summarization, so caching could help more than the sample showed. but curious about KV cache eviction and memory tradeoffs.
02:34 Ethan: eviction is LRU-ish and we can tune time-to-live and prefix length; more cache requires more memory on the worker and slightly higher idle cost but it's often worth it when hit-rate > ~20%.
02:44 Jordan: what about model variants, like 13B? we tried 13B locally.
02:48 Ethan: 13B gives better quality but cost goes up. our rough numbers: 13B quantized run gave ~60 tokens/sec single-stream and cost roughly ~$0.95 per 1M tokens -> tokens/sec per $1 is only ~63. So if you need higher quality on critical routes, route those to 13B and route bulk to 8B with cache + batching.
03:10 Carlos: that's a big delta; can Redwood do auto-routing based on route tags?
03:14 Maya: yes, smart routing is supported — you can set policies by latency / cost / region and we can do canary or percent-based splits.
03:22 Jordan: can you show the cost model spreadsheet now?
03:25 Ethan: sharing my screen — sorry small delay — okay open. so left column is route, next is calls per minute, avg tokens per call, cache hit assumptions, batching settings, model, and then estimated tokens per day and monthly spend.
03:40 Ethan: for route A (customer messages -> summarization) we set calls/min 120, avg tokens 450, we model 3 cache scenarios: 0%, 25%, 50% hit. at 25% hit with batch 4 for background compaction, monthly cost estimate drops by ~28% vs no cache.
03:58 Priya: these percentages assume perfect batching alignment; in reality users send single messages. so how do you simulate micro-batching?
04:06 Ethan: we approximate micro-batching by modeling our worker's continuous batching window (30-80ms) and simulated traffic bursts. for interactive flows micro-batching helps a little but most savings come from prefix caching for summaries.
04:18 Jordan: did you look at KV cache staleness risk? our summaries need fresh context.
04:22 Ethan: yes TTL and prefix length gating can mitigate that; for summaries we recommend short TTL (5-10m) and smaller prefix sizes so you don't serve stale consolidated data. also we surface cache hit metadata so you can audit when a response used cache.
04:36 Sofia: quick note — security folks ask about encryption of cached keys at rest and access logs. we can provide KMS integration and audit logs per request.
04:44 Priya: good, send the security doc.
04:46 Maya: will do. ok back to numbers — Jordan you mentioned long-tail prompts earlier; we need a traffic sample to refine numbers.
04:54 Jordan: yes I'll share top 50 routes and a histogram of tokens per call by Wed.
04:58 Maya: perfect. moving on, we wanted to propose an extended run — Ethan?
05:02 Ethan: the short runs gave us a baseline but to be confident on hit rates and batching impact we recommend a 24h benchmark using production-like request patterns, with 32MB prefix cache toggled on for half the test. we'll capture hit-rate, p50/p95 latencies per route, and cost estimates.
05:18 Carlos: how intrusive is that to our infra? will you need VPN?
05:22 Ethan: for Hosted API it's non-intrusive — we replay a synthetic stream from our test harness. if you want dedicated/private we may need peering but for this test hosted is OK and much faster to run.
05:34 Priya: sounds fine. any risk of data leakage in the logs? we need redaction.
05:38 Ethan: we can mask sensitive tokens and only store aggregate metrics; we also support PII redaction on ingest if you want.
05:46 Jordan: what's the expected cost delta if we go to dedicated pool? we are considering reserved capacity but want to see unit economics first.
05:52 Maya: Dedicated tends to lower unit cost at scale due to reserved pricing; example: our Dedicated 8B pool pricing could push cost per 1M tokens from $0.28 to ~$0.18 in these workloads depending on commit level. that improves tokens/sec per $1 accordingly. we'll include dedicated estimates in the spreadsheet.
06:10 Carlos: can you quantify break-even commit level?
06:12 Maya: with current traffic projections, a 3-6 month reserved commit at the anticipated throughput should break even vs hosted in ~2 months, but we'll model multiple commit sizes.
06:22 Jordan: what about quantization choices: 4-bit vs 8-bit? any quality regressions?
06:26 Ethan: 4-bit int4 gives bigger speedups but we saw occasional small quality regressions on summarization edge cases; int8/llm-int8 is a nice middle ground. for Lunaris we recommended trying int8 first for the initial pilot.
06:38 Priya: is the inference runtime compatible with our internal monitoring? we use Datadog and Prometheus.
06:42 Ethan: yes we have hooks and can emit Prom metrics and traces; we'll share the exporter config.
06:46 Jordan: after the 24h run, what are concrete success criteria?
06:50 Maya: main ones: cost-per-1M tokens reduction target (>=20% vs current baseline) with p95 latency within product SLOs (<250ms for interactive), and cache hit >25% on summarization routes.
06:58 Jordan: okay makes sense.
07:00 Priya: any notes on cold-start token penalty for big models? we saw large KV cache warms helping previously.
07:06 Ethan: yes warm cache reduces initial kv/kv overhead; our continuous batching and persistent worker pools help with cold starts. we'll capture cold-start rate in the 24h logs.
07:16 Sofia: quick admin: we'll send calendar invite for the extended run results review next Friday.
07:20 Maya: great. any final questions?
07:24 Carlos: just one — can you include an estimate for incremental storage cost for the 32MB prefix cache per worker?
07:30 Ethan: rough ballpark is +$0.015 per rcu-hour per worker in the dedicated sizing; we'll calculate properly and add to the sheet.
07:36 Jordan: thanks, that's helpful.
07:38 Maya: okay recap: Ethan runs 24h benchmark with and without 32MB cache, will capture hit-rates/latencies/cost. Maya will send updated cost model and security docs. Jordan will share traffic profile. schedule follow-up next Friday.
07:52 Jordan: thanks everyone.
07:54 Maya: thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional mis-transcribed technical names (Llama/Lama, KV vs K V). transcript clipped at 48m.
